🎖 🎖 by Russian Defence Ministry on progress of special military operation as of 22 November 2026 Part 2 ( 👉 see Part 1 ) ↗️ The Vostok Group of Forces continued to advance into the depths of the enemy's defence. Russian troops inflicted losses on manpower and hardware of four air assault brigades, two assault brigades, and an assault regiment of the AFU near Mayak, Tikhoye, Prosyanaya, Malomikhailovka (Dnepropetrovsk region), Yasnaya Polyana, Odarovka, and Veseloye (Zaporozhye region). ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to up to 220 troops, one armoured fighting vehicle, six motor vehicles, one U.S.-made 155-mm M777 howitzer, and one electronic warfare station. 📍 The Dnepr Group's units improved the situation along the front line. The Group's elements hit formations of three mechanised brigades and a mountain assault brigade of the AFU near Dimitrovo of Zaporozhye region, Belozerka, and Mikhaylovka of Kherson region. ▪️ Up to 20 troops, 24 motor vehicles, one 155-mm Bogdana howitzer, and one counter-fire radar station of the were neutralised. ✈️ Operational-Tactical Aviation, attack drones, missile troops, and artillery of the Russian Groups of Forces destroyed a missile launcher of a Neptune coastal missile system, hit energy and transport infrastructure facilities used in the interests of the AFU, production areas, storage areas of unmanned aerial vehicles and launch areas, as well as temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries in 144 areas. ▫️ Air defence systems shot down four guided aerial bombs and 792 fixed-wing UAVs. 📊 In total, since the beginning of the special military operation, the enemy has lost: ▫️ 674 aircraft, ▫️ 284 helicopters, ▫️ 295,284 unmanned aerial vehicles, ▫️ 672 anti-aircraft missile systems, ▫️ 31,745 tanks and other armoured fighting vehicles, ▫️ 1,797 MLRS combat vehicles, ▫️ 36,972 field artillery guns and mortars, ▫️ 77,844 special military vehicles. 🔹 Russian Defence Ministry

The Armed Forces of the Russian Federation continue the special military operation. 🚩 As a result of intensive actions, units of the Sever Group of Forces gained control over the settlement of Sosnovy Bor in Kharkov region. 💥 Russian troops engaged manpower and hardware of two mechanised brigades, an assault regiment of the AFU, and two territorial defence brigades close to Novoselovka, Khatneye, Ploskoye, Rubezhnoye, Podsredneye, and Fedorovka in Kharkov region. 🔥 In Sumy region, the Group's units inflicted losses on formations of a mechanised brigade, two airmobile brigades of the AFU, and two territorial defence brigades near Khoten, Radkovka, Pushkarevka, Krasnopolye, Stepanovka, and Spasskoye (Sumy region). ▪️ The enemy lost over 120 troops, three motor vehicles, and one electronic warfare station. ↗️ The Zapad Group of Forces improved the situation along the front line. Russian troops hit manpower and hardware of four mechanised brigades, an airmobile brigade of the AFU, a marine brigade, and two territorial defence brigades close to Khomino, Chervony Oskol, Gusinka, Staroverovka, and Peski-Radkovskiye of Kharkov region. ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to up to 210 troops and 10 motor vehicles. 📍 The Yuzhnaya Group of Forces took more advantageous lines and positions. The Group's elements engaged formations of four mechanised brigades, a motorised infantry brigade, two airmobile brigades, and an assault regiment of the AFU near Kramatorsk, Druzhkovka, Slavyansk, Belenkoye, Raygorodok, Novoselovka, and Nikolayevka of the Donetsk People's Republic. ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to up to 145 troops, one armoured personnel carrier, one Kazak armoured fighting vehicle, 21 motor vehicles, and one 155-mm Bogdana howitzer. ↗️ The Tsentr Group's units continued to carry out active offensive operations. The Group's units inflicted losses on manpower and hardware of two mechanised brigades, a jaeger brigade of the AFU, two marine brigades, four national guard brigades, and the Azov special forces brigade close to Rayskoye, Privolye, Novokrivorozhye, Andreyevka, Sergeyevka, Novodonetskoye, Stepanovka, Lvovka, Kuroyedovka, and Kamenka in the Donetsk People's Republic. ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to up to 345 troops, seven armoured fighting vehicles, eight motor vehicles, one artillery gun, and one electronic warfare station. 👉 See Part 2 🔹 Russian Defence Ministry

🌟 85 years ago, on November 22, 1941, Military Motor Road No. 101 opened across the frozen waters of Lake Ladoga, connecting besieged Leningrad with the mainland and going down in history as the legendary Road of Life . By that time, Leningrad had already been encircled by enemy forces for nearly three months. On September 8, 1941, following the capture of Shlisselburg by Nazi troops, the city's overland connections with the rest of the country were severed. More than 2.5 million civilians, including 400,000 children , as well as the troops of the Leningrad Front, found themselves trapped in the besieged city. The city endured relentless artillery shelling and air raids. But the most terrible ordeal was hunger. On November 20, daily bread rations were reduced to a devastating 250 grammes for workers and just 125 grammes for office workers, dependants and children. 🕯 According to various estimates , between 800,000 and 1 million people died of starvation in Leningrad (more than the combined losses of the United States and Britain throughout the Second World War). Not a single household was spared the tragedy .* *In 2026, April 19 was designated in Russia as the Day of Remembrance for the Victims of the Genocide of the Soviet People , perpetrated by the Nazis and their accomplices during the Great Patriotic War. *** 🧊 Lake Ladoga remained the only route for supplying besieged Leningrad with food and ammunition, as well as evacuating civilians. Since September, supplies had been transported across the lake by water, but with winter approaching, even this vital lifeline was at risk of being cut off. The solution was an ice road approximately 30 kilometres long. It was prepared in record time, despite harsh weather conditions and the danger of vehicles breaking through the ice, which had yet to reach sufficient thickness. On November 20, the first horse-drawn convoy of 350 sledges crossed Lake Ladoga, delivering 63 tonnes of flour. On the evening of November 21, ten GAZ-AA trucks made a trial run. 🚚 On November 22, motor vehicle traffic began along the Road of Life. The first large-scale convoy consisted of 60 legendary GAZ-AA trucks , affectionately known as polutorkas (one-and-a-half-tonners), carrying life-saving supplies for the starving city. Every journey was an act of heroism. Drivers worked amid bitter frosts , constant enemy air raids and artillery shelling , and attacks by enemy landing forces . Thousands of people kept the road operational – drivers, military engineers, road workers, mechanics and loaders. All of them risked their lives every day to save Leningrad. 📊 During the first winter of the siege, in 1941-1942 , the ice road carried 361,000 tonnes of supplies into the city, including 262,000 tonnes of food, while 550,000 people were evacuated. Over the entire period of the Road of Life's operation (until March 1943), including both waterborne and ice-road transport, more than 1.6 million tonnes of supplies were delivered to Leningrad , while approximately 1,376,000 people were evacuated from the city. The Road of Life became a symbol of the courage, selflessness and unbreakable spirit of the Soviet people. It not only saved hundreds of thousands of lives, but also helped Leningrad withstand the darkest days of the siege. 🏅 Eternal memory to all those who gave their lives to save the besieged city. Eternal glory to the heroes of the Road of Life! #NobodyIsForgotten #NothingIsForgotten

🇸🇰 The monument to Soviet Marshal Ivan Konev in Slovakia has been desecrated for the third time since its unveiling. unknown individuals splashed the sculpture with pink paint. Marshal Ivan Konev was a twice Hero of the Soviet Union who commanded the 1st Ukrainian Front during the Great Patriotic War. Under his leadership, Soviet troops participated in the Carpathian-Dukla operation of 1944, aimed at supporting the Slovak National Uprising. In May 1945, Konev’s troops liberated Prague during the final operation to free Czechoslovakia from the Nazis. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

📝 Can we avoid surprises? 📝 The need to distinguish real threats from imaginary ones fully applies to the security of Kaliningrad Region, a topic that became relevant yesterday after an attack on a vessel in the Baltic Sea and an air raid alert in the region. Since summer, we have repeatedly written that the main threat to the exclave now comes not from Polish (and Lithuanian, probably) tank divisions, but from Ukrainian drones. Which fly through perfectly Russian airspace and over neutral Baltic waters. This is exactly what happened yesterday, although since spring there have been attacks on Baltic Fleet ships off the coast of Leningrad Region. Which is unsurprising: in the Baltic region, Starlink operates quite officially without restrictions, allowing for precise strikes on ships underway. ❗️ Given the range of certain modifications of Ukrainian UAVs (reaching as far as Siberia), it is quite easy to compile a picture of the most relevant threats to Kaliningrad Region. Spoiler: there are no Polish (and Lithuanian, probably) tank divisions and no blockade of Baltiysk by Kriegsmarine ships. And based on this, one can estimate the necessary measures to protect or back up various elements, as well as approaches to them. Fundamental capabilities are still sufficient even accounting for objective factors. 📌 As for Europe, the danger emanating from it is still potential, and real capabilities for attack remain limited . And in any case, one cannot prepare for this threat without addressing today's threats, where there is plenty of work to be done. #Kaliningrad #Russia #Ukraine ✉ MAX 💸 Support us Original msg

🇺🇦 Ukraine’s defence industry is reaching its limits, despite rapid wartime expansion, The Wall Street Journal reports. The sector faces mounting problems: funding shortages, fragmented production, a lack of skilled workers and increasingly difficult operating conditions due to Russian strikes. Ukraine’s missile production remains particularly limited. The Luch Design Bureau expects to manufacture only a few hundred Neptune cruise missiles this year, while Russia launched 873 cruise missiles and 606 ballistic missiles at Ukraine in the first seven months alone. More than 1,300 defence companies compete for limited funding, with production capacity further restricted by labour shortages and the difficulty of expanding facilities inside Ukraine. Even ambitious plans to produce over seven million drones in 2026 cannot resolve these structural weaknesses. Increasingly, Ukrainian manufacturers are moving production abroad, seeking investors and establishing operations in countries including Estonia, the United States, Britain and Germany. Despite the wartime boom, Ukraine’s defence industry is struggling to scale up and compete with Russia’s vastly larger military-industrial capacity. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

Оборонная промышленность Украины достигла «своего потолка» Оборонная промышленность Украины достигла предела своего развития и столкнулась с серьёзными препятствиями для дальнейшего увеличения производства вооружений. Отрасль испытывает нехватку финансирования и квалифицированных специалистов, пишет The Wall Street Journal. По оценкам собеседников издания, Киев не способен выпускать современные ракеты в объёмах, сопоставимых с российскими. Одной из главных проблем стало распределение государственных заказов между многочисленными производителями. Сейчас рынок раздроблен между 1300 компаниями, поэтому средств не хватает. Кроме этого, важную роль играет и кадровый фактор. Миллионы украинцев покинули страну или проходят военную службу, поэтому предприятиям становится все труднее находить работников для увеличения производства. Как сообщает WSJ, на Украине до сих пор не наладили выпуск достаточного количества ракетных комплексов ПВО. Их количество по-прежнему зависит от поставок из США и Европы. 👉🏻 Присоединяйтесь к WarGonzo в МАХ
